description.p: Murmel is a GTK4/Libadwaita Mumble client for GNOME. It lets you join Mumble servers, chat with text messages, and talk with voice — with low-latency Opus audio and automatic reconnection.

ul.li: Native GTK4 / Libadwaita design following the GNOME HIG
Responsive layout: works on mobile and desktop
Voice activation with a live level meter, noise suppression and echo cancellation
Adjustable voice quality and device selection
Saved connections with passwords in the keyring
Client certificates and trust-on-first-use server certificates
Notifications and sounds for messages and users joining or leaving
mumble:// links

ul.li: Dark mode: choose Follow System, Light or Dark in Preferences → Behavior

Create certificates in the app: from the connect dialog (+ next to the certificate) or in Preferences → Identity, which now lists all certificates with export and delete; Murmel offers to back up a new certificate
When a server needs a certificate (for example to register your name), Murmel offers to create one and reconnects with it
Fixed logging in with a registered name on Mumble 1.6 servers that have a server password
A name registered with another certificate is explained instead of asking for a password again and again
The chat starts empty for each new connection; after an automatic reconnect it is kept and the welcome message is not repeated
The microphone, headphone and level buttons line up with the message field
Avatars: users' uploaded pictures are shown in the channel list, round like the initials shown otherwise; set your own avatar per saved connection or a default one in Preferences

New channel editor (Edit… in the channel menu) with pages for name, position, user limit and password; the description with a formatting toolbar and live preview; groups; and permissions with allow, deny or inherit per right
Channels with a password ask for it when you join

The voice level is shown as thin waves: green while you are heard, yellow while your voice is detected but not sent (muted or not connected), red when too loud; it works from the start, before connecting
While you are muted and speak, the crossed-out microphone next to your name lights up yellow
The connect dialog shows more saved connections and makes clear that the list scrolls
Identities can be imported and exported in Preferences
Channel names line up whether or not a channel has users, and avatars line up with them
Fixed rare crashes when the server changed users or channels while you clicked
Fixed the root channel's permissions never loading
New chat layout: private messages open in their own view when you click a user, with unread badges next to names in the channel list
Event lines in the channel chat (users joining or leaving, moves, mutes), configurable on the new Chat page in Preferences
Formatted messages and images: bold and italic buttons (Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I) and an image button that fits pictures to the server limit; received formatting, links and images are shown
The channel description appears at the top of the channel chat, collapsed with a "Show more" button; a description starting with a wide image shows it as a banner behind the header
Microphone, headphones and level meter moved to the bottom of the channel list; the connection dot sits in the top corner and the server name is the title
Collapsing a channel also hides its users
Fixed image messages being silently dropped by the server
Added echo cancellation for speakers instead of a headset (off by default)
Noise suppression and echo cancellation can also be set in the waveform popover, next to the activation threshold
Screenshots in the software center
mumble:// links open the connect dialog with the link's server and user filled in, and join the linked channel
Disconnect from the main menu; quitting while connected asks for confirmation
Ban list and registered users work and only appear while connected
Context menu entries follow your permissions on the server
A password the server asks for (e.g. SuperUser) is requested and can be remembered in the keyring
User statistics: version, connection, ping and packet counters
Register is only offered when it is possible (requires a certificate)
Context menus look the same in every row
Fixed voice activation: the threshold now works directly and is set on a live level meter, and the click at the start of speech is gone
Fixed audio latency problems: playback no longer stalls USB headsets that cannot handle very small buffers
Added noise suppression for the microphone
Added an adjustable voice quality (32–192 kb/s), limited to the server's bandwidth
New About dialog with version, website and issue tracker
Event sounds with per-event choice in Preferences
Sort POT inputs so the check is deterministic
Even status bar spacing in the window corner
User join/leave notifications; pad the app icon
Waveform opens the activation threshold popover
Configurable jitter buffer and audio per packet
Status dot with connection details tooltip
Save connections; pick saved servers in the dialog
Play incoming packets larger than 10 ms; log received voice
Raise the playback buffer when the output device stalls
Log server version, bandwidth and voice delivery stats
Mix incoming voice, copy outgoing frames, speaking indicators
Crisp voice meter rendering
Join channels on double-click; restyle voice meter
Capture and play through separate streams
Device pickers, threshold popover and voice meter
Show all channels, highlight current channel, usable composer
Announce client version 1.4.0 (P11)
Show successful connections in the UI
Build Flatpak on GNOME 51 with D-Bus service file
Rename to Murmel, NavigationSplitView shell, richer connect dialog
